headline: iOS 17 adds convenient new iPhone clipboard paste feature
summary: Apple's latest iOS update introduces a handy clipboard paste functionality, streamlining how users transfer information between apps on their iPhones.
details: iOS 17 brings a significant quality-of-life improvement for iPhone users with a new clipboard pasting feature. This addition aims to make transferring text and data between applications more efficient and intuitive.

The new functionality allows users to quickly paste content directly from their clipboard without needing to navigate through multiple menus or apps. This is particularly useful for tasks that involve frequent copying and pasting of information.

While the exact implementation details are still emerging, the core benefit is a smoother workflow for users who rely on their iPhone for productivity tasks. This feature is expected to be a frequently used addition for many.

The update is part of Apple's ongoing efforts to enhance the user experience on its devices, focusing on small but impactful changes that improve daily usability. iOS 17 is set to roll out to compatible iPhone models soon.

headline_marked: Samsung's [[new smart glasses]] boast 9-hour battery life
headline: Samsung's new smart glasses boast 9-hour battery life
summary: Samsung has revealed its upcoming smart glasses, featuring two new designs and an impressive 9-hour battery life. Developed with Google, Gentle Monster, and Warby Parker, they are set to launch this fall.
details: Samsung has provided a first look at its upcoming smart glasses, showcasing two new designs and revealing key specifications, including a battery life that surpasses Meta's offerings. These glasses, a collaboration between Samsung, Google, Gentle Monster, and Warby Parker, are slated for release this fall.

Following teasers and initial reveals at Google I/O, two additional frame styles have emerged: a boxy black design from Gentle Monster and a more rounded red-brown pair from Warby Parker. Samsung's mobile experience division executive vice president, Jaein Choi, indicated that more designs are planned.

These frames are notably lightweight, comparable to standard thick-rimmed glasses. Integrated speakers and microphones are discreetly housed in the stems, with a single button on the right and a power switch on the left. A camera and recording LED are positioned on the front, aiming for a design that looks like normal eyewear.

Powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 chip, the same processor used in Meta's latest smart glasses, Samsung's glasses promise up to nine hours of use on a single charge. The accompanying charging case provides an additional seven charges.

Users can interact with the glasses using either Google Gemini or Samsung's Bixby. The AI features include message summaries, live translation, navigation assistance, and camera-based analysis or descriptions.

Similar to Meta's smart glasses, a recording LED is present when the camera is active. Choi stated that the glasses will disable recording if the LED is detected as blocked, addressing privacy concerns that have previously led to similar devices being criticized.
